story_ai.headline: Sensex, Nifty scale multi-month closing highs as tariff fears ease
paragraphs: GIFT Nifty is at 25955, implying a positive start for the Indian market with an estimated gap up of 70.5 points compared to the previous Nifty close of 25884.5.

Overnight global markets presented a mixed picture as US indices finished on varied notes with the S&P 500 down -0.25%, Nasdaq down -0.62%, and Dow Jones up 0.33%, while US futures currently trade higher led by Nasdaq futures up 2.07%. Across Asia, indices are posting gains with Nikkei 225 up 1.17%, Kospi up 2.69%, and Hang Seng up 0.84%, following strong rallies in Europe where the DAX gained 2.08% and the FTSE 100 rose 1.75%.

In commodities, Brent crude trades higher at 92.23 and WTI crude is at 85.73, while gold stands at 3651.1 and copper trades at 5.64. In currency and rates, USD/INR is at 92.435, the dollar index is at 103.684, and the US 10Y yield is at 4.848, with India VIX dropping -4.88% to 16.81.

Foreign Institutional Investors continue to record activity in the cash market, with provisional data showing net purchases of Rs 5843.33 crore alongside Domestic Institutional Investors buying Rs 5630.72 crore. Options positioning for the upcoming expiry shows call walls clustered heavily at the 26000 strike with 10938330.0 open interest, while put walls are active around the 25000 strike.

On the corporate and events calendar, SETCO reports results today, while Mahanadi Coalfields makes its Mumbai debut following a $969 million IPO and Airpro Technology opens its IPO. F&O ban list features APLAPOLLO and MANAPPURAM.

Key news highlights include Sensex and Nifty scaling multi-month closing highs as tariff fears ease, alongside developments around Thomas Cook facing NCLT creditor meetings and Urban Company starting pre-bookings for residential ACs, touching sectors from broad markets and financial services to consumer services.
